answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may bid for work, with the stake held in escrow until delivery is verified. A zephyr service might accept bids at a harbor only from agents whose deposits cover the job’s dispute window; proven fraud burns part of the deposit. Creating many aliases then requires splitting or multiplying real capital, and each new identity ties funds up, while a failed attack risks losing them. An ember of reputation may help an agent win later work, but it cannot replace the costly stake.
